syscheck.d.accounts: Accounts without required two-factor authentication, locked accounts, unused temporary passwords.
syscheck.d.analyst: Whether the scheduled analysis is ready, ran on time and finished without error.
syscheck.d.anchor_file: The anchors must be in an append-only file (chattr +a), which the service cannot alter.
syscheck.d.apply: The root program that writes the managed rule files; "edited outside" means a file was changed without going through this system.
syscheck.d.audit_chain: Hash chain of the audit log and its anchors.
syscheck.d.blocks: The block list is loaded by nginx, matches the database, and is below 80% of the limit.
syscheck.d.body_inspection: A request body larger than SecRequestBodyLimit (a file upload) or SecRequestBodyNoFilesLimit (a form or JSON, 128 KB by default), or one ModSecurity cannot parse, is passed on with none of it inspected while the engine is DetectionOnly (this system blocks with ctl:ruleEngine=On in its rules, so SecRequestBodyLimitAction Reject never rejects). Measured with libmodsecurity 3.0.9, 3.0.14 and 3.0.17: no rule sees any part of such a body. The sites listed take such bodies with no rule for it: propose a confident block on "Request body not inspected" (the protection sets include one; list the paths that take large uploads as exceptions), or raise SecRequestBodyLimit if the host's memory allows (see "Large uploads and memory").
syscheck.d.changes: Changes waiting more than 3 days for approval, or stuck in checking or applying for over an hour.
syscheck.d.config_changes: Changes to nginx / ModSecurity / CRS files made outside the change workflow in the last 7 days.
syscheck.d.countries: The regional registry lists are recent, the last download worked, and the lists in use were written.
syscheck.d.crs: Whether the daily CRS check ran in the last 3 days without error, and no other updater runs on this host.
syscheck.d.database: Size, schema version and SQLite consistency check.
syscheck.d.disk: Free space where the database lives.
syscheck.d.dns: Internal and external DNS servers are set, the check ran on time, and every server answered.
syscheck.d.geoip: Whether the country / network owner databases are installed and the last update worked.
syscheck.d.health: After each apply the program compares these URLs before and after; without any, a broken site is not noticed.
syscheck.d.intel: The second-tier LLM is set up, searched recently without error, is within its token limits, has a confirmed list of web applications, and no exploited vulnerability that affects this site is still open.
syscheck.d.jobs: Every installed timer and path unit is enabled; one that is not never runs.
syscheck.d.logrotate: Something rotates the ModSecurity audit log; otherwise it grows until the disk is full.
syscheck.d.modsecurity: The engine mode, the CRS found, and settings this program needs (JSON audit log, audit engine on).
syscheck.d.nginx_module: Whether the installed nginx loads the ModSecurity module (loaded once with a throwaway configuration), and whether the next system update would leave the module behind nginx (from the package lists apt already has; nothing downloaded).
syscheck.d.notify: Whether notifications are on, which channels are in use, failures in the last 24 hours, and whether the queue is stuck (the sender is not running).
syscheck.d.program_integrity: Installed files against the signed release manifest (SHA-256 of every file, RSA signature, pinned key).
syscheck.d.syslog: Every audit record and anchor is also sent to syslog for the SIEM.
syscheck.d.time_sync: The system clock must be synchronised (NTP): audit times come from it.
syscheck.d.tokens: Tokens that expire within 30 days, and tokens not used for 90 days (consider revoking them).
syscheck.d.traffic: The access logs are found and readable, and the counts are recent.
syscheck.d.upload_memory: nginx's ModSecurity module reads a whole upload into memory before ModSecurity sees it, whatever the body limits say (a 1 GB upload over the inspection limit took an nginx worker to 1.6-1.9 GB; without ModSecurity, 8 MB). The part ModSecurity inspects (up to SecRequestBodyLimit) costs much more, and is slow: measured with the CRS 4.30 on an 8 GB host, 256 MB took 2.1 GB at about 4 MB/s and 512 MB took 4.2 GB. A site with ModSecurity on whose largest upload, counted this way, is over half of this host's memory (or that accepts any size, 0) can have nginx stopped for every site by one large upload. Lower its client_max_body_size or SecRequestBodyLimit, or switch ModSecurity off only for a location that takes nothing but uploads.

uiset.group.analyst.hint: Reviews recent events with the self-hosted LLM for attack probes and false positives, proposes confident blocks or exclusions, and opens alerts for what needs following up. Loosening always needs your approval; whether confident blocks apply by themselves is set under the change workflow.
uiset.group.blocks.hint: An nginx deny list for every site. Turn this on only after nginx includes the list file inside http { } (the Blocked IPs page shows the line and checks it).
uiset.group.countries.hint: Per-site limits by country (only some countries, or not some countries). Each site's limit is a rule that goes through the change workflow; the lists are refreshed daily.
uiset.group.dns.hint: Which site names your internal and external DNS servers know, and the PTR names of outside addresses. A separate restricted job asks the servers; the web service never does.

uiset.group.intel.hint: A stronger LLM, local or cloud, that searches the web for new vulnerabilities in the confirmed web applications. Only product names, versions and a few host facts are sent. Leave the URL empty to use the first-tier LLM server.
uiset.group.iprep.hint: Is an outside address known to be malicious? Public lists downloaded once a day and matched on this host, Shodan InternetDB and your own MISP, put together on the IP lookup with what this site saw. Only a separate unit connects out; nothing is blocked by itself.
uiset.group.llm.hint: Used by the scheduled event analysis and by the "AI analysis" button on an event; request data stays in your network. OpenAI-compatible API (base URL ends in /v1). The web service connects only when you press Test. Recommended: an instruction model of about 14B parameters or more at 4-bit quantization or better, a context of at least 16k tokens, and a server that supports JSON schema answers (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama).
uiset.group.n_discord.hint: Discord channel settings > Integrations > Webhooks. Messages never trigger mentions.
uiset.group.n_email.hint: Sent over SMTP as plain text plus HTML.
uiset.group.n_nextcloud.hint: Install a bot with occ talk:bot:install and enter the Nextcloud URL, the conversation token and the bot secret (messages are signed with HMAC).
uiset.group.n_teams.hint: In the Teams channel, create a Workflows flow "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" and paste its URL. Messages are sent as Adaptive Cards.
uiset.group.n_telegram.hint: Create a bot with @BotFather, add it to the group or channel, then enter the bot token and the chat id.
uiset.group.n_webhook.hint: POSTs JSON to your URL (n8n, your own program...). With a signing secret, X-Jt-Waf-Mgr-Signature is sha256=HMAC(secret, timestamp + "." + body); the timestamp is in X-Jt-Waf-Mgr-Timestamp.
uiset.group.n_zulip.hint: Create a bot in Zulip and enter the site, the bot e-mail and API key, the channel and the topic.
uiset.group.nginxup.hint: Every 6 hours apt's lists for nginx's repository are refreshed and the next nginx is tried with the ModSecurity module; nginx.org's security advisories are read at the same time.
uiset.group.notify.hint: Important events (security, changes, analysis, system) go to the channels set up below. The web service only queues them; a separate sender service sends them, retries failures and reminds open alerts.
uiset.group.policy.hint: Applies to new logins and password changes from now on.
uiset.group.review.hint: Every few hours: was anybody blocked by mistake, new internal hits, outside attacks that got through, what was done automatically, one line per focus site. Sent through the notification channels (event "Periodic WAF review").
uiset.group.syslog.hint: Every audit record and anchor goes out as one JSON line for the SIEM. Keeping the local /dev/log and letting the host's rsyslog forward it is recommended; to send to a remote host directly, the web service (allowed to reach localhost only) needs that address in its systemd unit first (systemctl edit, IPAddressAllow=address).
uiset.group.traffic.hint: Counts the requests in the nginx access logs per site and hour (numbers only), so the WAF figures have a total to compare with. The site is taken from the file name (<site>.access.log).
uiset.group.warroom.hint: Where the events arrive on the maps (the WAF's public location, city level is enough) and how long each page stays when rotating. Without a location the maps show the sources only.
uiset.hub.enabled: Sync the CrowdSec Hub rules daily
uiset.integrity.automation_paths.hint: Absolute paths or patterns (*), for example the CRS update and the country lists. Changes there are recorded as automation, not as outside changes.
uiset.intel.backend_versions.hint: nginx does not pass a back-end server's Server header on, so the nginx, Apache or PHP version a back-end host runs cannot be seen from outside. When on, before each search the threat-intelligence program sends one GET / (with the site's name; only the answer's headers are read, not its content) to each private address the nginx configuration's proxy_pass points to, reads the product and version from Server and X-Powered-By, and lists them in the software list (marked "back-end host"). A back-end nginx is compared with nginx.org's security advisories, with an alert when it is affected (that host is not updated from here). waf.guide_link_d: See which mechanisms block, which only log and at which score — drawn from the configuration in effect.
waf.intro: Drawn from the configuration that is in effect now (nginx + ModSecurity files): which mechanisms exist, which of them block, which only log or add score, and which loosen the checks — for requests from outside and from the internal networks.
waf.note.eval_mixed: blocks only when an earlier rule turned blocking on for the request ({ids}); otherwise only logs.
waf.note.logs: the engine is {mode} for this source here, so a deny is only logged.
waf.note.not_applicable: the rules' source condition excludes this source.
waf.note.not_reached: the rules only act on a mark that no rule sets for this source.
waf.note.switched: blocking is turned on for single requests by rule(s) {ids}.
waf.redirect_hint: This block only sends clients elsewhere (http to https): nothing in it for the WAF to protect.
waf.score.hint: Each CRS match adds points by severity. A request is judged against the threshold {n}; the bars show how many matches of one severity reach it.
waf.score.legend_below: one match, still under the threshold
waf.score.legend_reach: the match that reaches the threshold
waf.score.levels_note: Counted from the rule files: rules with a severity, by their paranoia-level tag.
waf.score.title: Anomaly score
waf.stage.confident.desc: Site rules for requests that are certainly attacks (a path, a file name, a header…), usually limited to some sources. When one matches it marks the request and turns blocking on for that request only, so the CRS decision or the fallback rule refuses it.
waf.stage.crs_detect.desc: The CRS rules of the active paranoia level look for attack patterns. Every match adds points by its severity; nothing is blocked in this step.
waf.stage.crs_eval.desc: CRS compares the total inbound anomaly score with the threshold ({n}). At or over it the rule denies — but a deny only blocks when the engine is On for that request; with {mode} it is only logged.
waf.stage.deny_rules.desc: Other rules with deny (for example ModSecurity's own request body checks). They block only when the engine is On for the request; otherwise they only log.
waf.stage.engine.desc: SecRuleEngine decides whether a deny really blocks: DetectionOnly only logs, On blocks. A rule can switch it on for one request (ctl:ruleEngine=On) and a vhost can set its own mode.
waf.stage.exclusions.desc: Rules that make the WAF less strict for some requests: they remove CRS rules or inspected fields (ctl:ruleRemove…, SecRuleRemoveById, SecRuleUpdateTargetById), switch body inspection off, allow, enable exclusion plugins or widen the allowed methods and types. They run first (or when the configuration is loaded), so the later steps never see what they removed.
waf.stage.fallback.desc: A deny for requests an earlier rule marked (for example a confident match whose score stayed under the threshold).
waf.stage.not_inspected.desc: Requests to vhosts without the WAF, to locations with "modsecurity off", or after a rule turned the engine Off never reach the checks below: nothing is scored, logged or blocked.
waf.stage.other.desc: Site rules this diagram cannot classify. Check their id and message in the table.
waf.stage.outcome.desc: What happens to a request from each source in the end.
waf.stage.settings.desc: Rules that change settings for some requests (thresholds, paranoia level, body processor). They do not block by themselves.
waf.stage.site_scoring.desc: Site rules that add anomaly points (for example the points of a confident match), so that the CRS threshold check decides.
waf.stage.threshold_block.desc: Site rules after CRS that read the CRS score themselves: when it reached the threshold (and the source matches their condition) they turn blocking on and refuse the request, even though the global engine only logs.
waf.sum.blocked_score: blocked when the anomaly score reaches {n} (refused by rule {by})
waf.sum.confident: also blocked at once when one of {n} confident block rules matches
waf.sum.context: {n} vhost(s) set their own engine mode {mode} ({names}): external {ext}, internal {int}.
waf.sum.enabled_by: , after rule {ids} turned blocking on for that request
waf.sum.logged_only: never blocked; logged as over the threshold when the score reaches {n}.
waf.sum.mismatch: {n} site rule(s) use an internal address list that differs from this system's internal networks ({ids}); addresses missing from their list are treated as external there.
waf.sum.not_inspected: Not inspected at all: {v} vhost(s) without the WAF and {l} location(s) with modsecurity off.
waf.sum.title: In short
waf.sum.unclassified: {n} site rule(s) could not be classified ({ids}); see "Other site rules" in the table.
waf.sum.weakens: Some exclusions remove blocking rules for the requests they match: {list}.

wizard.arg_name_note: Parameter names in the query string and the body (forms, multipart upload parts) are compared in lower case: write the regular expression in lower case, anchored with ^ and $. Request bodies are not in the access logs, so the evidence check cannot look for it there.
wizard.arg_note: The value of this one parameter, in the query string or a form body, is compared in lower case: write the regular expression in lower case. A JSON body's top-level key is named json.<key>. Request bodies are not in the access logs, so the evidence check cannot look for it there.
wizard.before_rule_id_hint: Rule ID of a managed rule in the same file. Empty: at the end of the file. Order matters when a later rule reads what this one sets (e.g. before 10299, which refuses requests marked for blocking).
wizard.block_intro: Blocks external requests matching a clear attack shape. Internal sources are never blocked; CRS's 949110 takes the decision.
wizard.block_source_all_note: Internal sources are blocked too. The evidence check fails if any internal address other than a known scanner made such a request, and this change is never applied automatically. The known scanner list is written into the rule as it is now; after changing the list, propose the rule again.
wizard.body_unchecked_note: No pattern: matches a request whose body ModSecurity did not inspect, because it was over SecRequestBodyLimit / SecRequestBodyNoFilesLimit or could not be parsed. List the paths that take large uploads as exceptions. The access log has no request bodies, so the evidence check cannot look for it.
wizard.confirm_tag: I understand that a whole rule class is switched off here
wizard.country_intro: Limit one site by where requests come from: only the countries you list, or every country except them. The address lists come from the five regional Internet registries and are refreshed daily.
wizard.country_limits: Registry data says where an address block was registered, not where its user is (a VPN, a cloud region or a roaming phone can be elsewhere). It works through ModSecurity: locations with modsecurity off are not covered. Behind a CDN the site needs set_real_ip_from / real_ip_header.
wizard.country_never: Never refused: the internal networks, the known scanners, the trusted proxies and the protected list (Settings > Temporary IP blocks), so a CDN in front of the site is not shut out.
wizard.country_no_data: The country lists have not been downloaded yet. Use "Update now" in Settings, then try again.
wizard.exceptions: Exceptions (paths, one regular expression per line)
wizard.exceptions_hint: For example WebDAV or share links, where sync clients legitimately fetch .env or .git files.
wizard.exclusion_intro: Narrowest first: one site, one path, one rule, one field. The rule keeps protecting everything else.
wizard.external_only: Applies to external sources only; internal sources are only logged.
wizard.kind: What do you want to do?
wizard.kind_hint.confident_block: An attack shape: block it for external sources, with evidence that no one legitimate is hit.
wizard.kind_hint.country: Where requests come from: one site only for some countries, or not for some countries.
wizard.kind_hint.exclusion: A false positive: stop one rule from looking at one thing, as narrowly as possible.
wizard.kind_hint.plugin: Turn on a CRS plugin (WordPress, Nextcloud…) for one site.
wizard.kind_hint.raw: Write a SecRule yourself (administrators only, checked against a forbidden list).
wizard.kind_hint.redaction: Passwords and secrets: never inspected, so never copied into the audit log.
wizard.loosen_note: This change loosens the WAF: a person has to approve it, whatever the checks say.
wizard.lowercase_note: Matched after lowercasing (and, for paths, URL-decoding and normalizing): write the expression in lowercase.
wizard.plugin_intro: CRS plugins are off by default and turned on per site.
wizard.preview_empty: Fill in the form to see the generated rule.
wizard.raw_warning: Expert mode: the text is used as written. Engine-wide settings, audit settings, Include, exec, file operators and removing system rules are refused.
wizard.reason_ph: What happened, which evidence, why this is the narrowest change
wizard.redaction_intro: These fields are never inspected by CRS, so their values never end up in the audit log.
wizard.remove_tag_warning: Warning: this switches off an entire class of rules (for example every SQL injection rule) for these requests. Use it only if field-level exclusions cannot work.
wizard.score_only_explain: Use for endpoints whose body is what people type: saving drafts, sending mail or chat messages. Code, paths and commands there are normal and should not get a user blocked by the anomaly score.
wizard.submit_hint: Static check, evidence and sandbox run next; then it waits for approval.
wizard.tests_hint.block: At least one external request that must be blocked (403). Encoding, case and slash variants and the same request from an internal source are added automatically, plus each site's regression samples.
wizard.tests_hint.country: Tests are added for you: a request from a country that passes, one from a country that is refused, and one from inside.
wizard.tests_hint.other: Replay the request that caused the false positive; list the excluded rules under "Rules that must not match".
